content.text:
This is confirmed, documented behavior, not a bug.

Per `content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows.md`, section **`schedule`** → **`actor` for scheduled workflows**: scheduled workflows run as the `actor` who last modified the cron syntax. If that user's account is deleted, there's no valid actor, so the workflow stops running. Notifications for scheduled workflows also only go to that same user (per the linked "notifications for workflow runs" doc), which explains why no one else was alerted.

Fix: have another repo collaborator with write access make any commit changing the workflow's cron line — this reassigns the `actor` to them and reactivates the schedule.
